title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
statement:
You are given two arrays `nums1` and `nums2`, each sorted in non-decreasing order. Either may be empty, but not both.

Return the **median** of all `m + n` values taken together, as a `double`. With an odd total that's the middle value; with an even total it's the average of the two middle values.

Aim for **O(log(m + n))** time — merging the arrays works but isn't what the interviewer is after.

target.note: O(log(min(m, n))). Logarithmic time can't be told apart from linear at these sizes, so there's no benchmark — an O(m + n) merge passes the tests, but the interview wants the partition search

hints: The median splits the combined values into a left half and a right half of equal size. If you knew how many of the left half came from nums1, how many would come from nums2?

Choose i elements from nums1 and j = half - i from nums2 for the left half. The split is correct exactly when nums1[i-1] <= nums2[j] and nums2[j-1] <= nums1[i]. Each violated condition tells you which way to move i, so binary search on i.

Binary search i over 0..m on the shorter array, with j = (m + n + 1) / 2 - i, treating out-of-range neighbours as -infinity / +infinity. If nums1[i-1] > nums2[j], move left; if nums2[j-1] > nums1[i], move right. Once balanced, the median is max(left maxes) for an odd total, or the average of max(left maxes) and min(right mins) for an even one.
followups: Generalize it: find the k-th smallest element of two sorted arrays in O(log k).
Why does searching the shorter array matter, both for speed and for keeping j in range?
How would you find the median of k sorted arrays, or of a stream of numbers?
explain: Instead of merging, search for the partition. Let half = (m + n + 1) / 2 be the size of the combined left half. If the left half takes i elements from nums1, it must take j = half - i from nums2. The partition is valid when every left value is <= every right value, which, because both arrays are sorted, reduces to nums1[i-1] <= nums2[j] and nums2[j-1] <= nums1[i]. If nums1[i-1] is too big, i must shrink; if nums2[j-1] is too big, i must grow — so binary search i on the shorter array. Missing neighbours at the edges count as -infinity and +infinity. Then the median is the larger left-side value (odd total) or the average of that and the smaller right-side value (even total). O(log(min(m, n))) time, O(1) space. Java details: use long sentinels (or Integer.MIN_VALUE/MAX_VALUE carefully), and add the two middle values as longs before dividing by 2.0, since two ints near 2^31 overflow.
